# Backend Data TODO

This document tracks every hardcoded mock value in the Analysis Player and the API shape needed to make it real.

All mock data lives in `src/mocks/fightMock.ts` and is consumed by the components in `src/components/player/`.

---

## 1. Fighter Profiles

**Hardcoded in:** `src/mocks/fightMock.ts` → `fighters.red` / `fighters.blue`

**Consumed by:** `FighterColumn.tsx`, `MatchupCard.tsx`, `Momentum.tsx`

**Missing from API:** The backend has no concept of fighter identity beyond `fighter_id` (0 = red, 1 = blue in the overlay). Needed fields per fighter:

```ts
interface FighterProfile {
  fighter_id: number;   // 0 | 1
  name: string;         // e.g. "BATUR"
  first: string;        // first name
  nickname: string;
  record: string;       // "14-3-0"
  country: string;      // ISO 3-letter
  corner: 'red' | 'blue';
  reach: string;        // e.g. '74"'
  height: string;       // e.g. "6'1\""
  age: number;
}
```

**Suggested endpoint:** `GET /fights/{id}/fighters` → `FighterProfile[]`

---

## 2. Per-Round Aggregated Stats Per Fighter

**Status:** Resolved client-side — `deriveStatsForRange()` in `src/utils/liveStats.ts` parses
`events` (frame-filtered to the whole fight, a round's `[start_frame, end_frame]`, or
`[0, currentFrame]` for "Live") and is consumed by `FightStatistics.tsx` for all three

content.text: This is a big ask — the mockup's clip player is synthetic pose animation and its "flags" are simulated defects, but the real app has actual video, real fighter-frame boxes, and real label events (`fight_events` with `source='label'`). Two architecture calls will shape the whole build, so I want to confirm before committing:

questions.question: The mockup's verdicts (Confirm/Decline per event) aren't backed by anything in the DB today. How should Training Data QA persist them?

options.label: localStorage only (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the mockup exactly, ships today with zero backend work. Verdicts live per-browser, not shared across reviewers or persisted server-side — same tradeoff the prototype itself made.

options.label: New backend field + endpoint
options.description: Add a real 'qa_verdict' column/table on fight_events (or a side table) plus an API to set it. Durable and shareable, but a real backend migration + endpoint, well beyond a frontend page.

questions.question: The mockup plays a synthesized fake skeleton animation per event ('Synthesised from exported keypoints'). The real app already has actual video + real FighterOverlay boxes for real frames. What should the clip player show?

options.label: Real video scrub (Recommended)
options.description: Reuse VideoPlayer + FighterOverlay, scrubbed to a short window around the event's real frame, with real fighter-box overlays. True to the actual data, but no per-event confidence/keypoint data exists to draw a skeleton or synthesize defects.

options.label: Keep the synthetic skeleton clip
options.description: Port the mockup's SkeletonClip pose-synthesis engine as-is. Visually matches the design exactly but the motion and 'defect' flags (dropped limb, jitter, low confidence) are entirely fabricated, not derived from real data.

questions.question: The mockup's 'automatic checks' (low keypoint confidence, corner swap, jitter, etc.) are randomly generated per event — there's no real signal to compute them from today. What should happen to that panel?

options.label: Drop it for now (Recommended)
options.description: Show 'No automatic checks run yet' instead of fake flags — matches the PipelineAccuracy precedent of only showing what's honestly measurable, and documents the gap in TODO_BACKEND_DATA.md.

options.label: Derive a partial version
options.description: Flag only what's actually computable now, e.g. events inside an open/confirmed corner_swap span (utils/cornerSwap.ts) — real but much thinner than the mockup's 6 defect types.

## Training Data QA (`TrainingDataQA.tsx`)

`/training-data` is a reviewer's pass over every hand-labelled point event that is an actual training class (`utils/trainingDataTaxonomy.ts`'s `TRAINING_CLASSES` — the `needsFighter` items of Annotate's `TOOL_GROUPS`, minus `takedown_attempt`/`takedown_defended`/`submission_attempt`/`knockdown`/every `state_*` mark), across **every** labelled fight at once — the one page in this app that isn't scoped to a single `fightId`. `useTrainingDataEvents()` fetches every `training_data`/`reference` fight that has reached Annotate (`state` in `labeling_in_progress`/`labeling_complete`), then that fight's `source='label' kind='point'` events, tags each with its own `fight`, and filters to `TRAINING_ACTIONS`.

**Three-level client-side navigation**, all local `view` state in `TrainingDataQA.tsx` (no routing): classes (`ClassGrid`) → one class's events (`EventTable`, filterable by verdict/fight) → one event's review (`EventReview`). A "done" screen appears once every event in a class has a verdict.

**`ClipPlayer.tsx` plays the real video, not a synthesised clip.** Unlike the design mockup this page is built from (which rendered a fabricated pose-animation "clip" with fabricated defect flags — see the project's `Training Data.html`/`td-data.js`), there is no per-event confidence/keypoint-quality signal to synthesise from, so the "automatic checks" panel from that mockup was deliberately dropped rather than faked. `ClipPlayer` instead reuses the same `requestVideoFrameCallback` draw loop as `Player.tsx`, scoped to a ~2.4s window (`CLIP_HALF_WINDOW_SECS = 1.2`) around the event's real frame, looping automatically during playback, with the real `FighterOverlay` (boxes + skeletons, `highlightCorner` = the label's own `corner`, corner-swap-aware) drawn on top — same frame-numbering contract as everywhere else (`Math.floor(t * fps) + 1`).
